name: Katana MRP
summary: Cloud manufacturing and inventory platform for product businesses. Live inventory control, production scheduling and order syncing across your sales channels — know exactly what to make and when.
best_for: product makers and small manufacturers who need live inventory, production scheduling and multi-channel order sync in one cloud platform
skip_if: you're a simple reseller who doesn't manufacture (a plain inventory tool is cheaper), or you need a published monthly price to compare before talking to sales
honest_knock: There is no public price above Free any more. Since late October 2026 the pricing page lists only Free (30 SKUs) and Advantage, a custom annual contract quoted after a scoping call, so you cannot set Katana's cost against an alternative until you have been through sales. It is capable manufacturing software and the quote bundles the modules that used to be paid add-ons; ask for the quote in writing, with the contract term and what changes if your SKU count or order volume grows.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-30 on katanamrp.com/pricing) The public pricing page now shows two packages. Free costs $0 with no card: up to 30 SKUs, unlimited users, integrations and inventory locations, all Katana features and API access, with support through the AI assistant and knowledge base; the FAQ adds that the first 15 days allow unlimited SKUs and that Shopify is currently the only e-commerce integration that works on Free. Advantage has no published price: Katana scopes your setup and quotes one price under a custom annual contract, which the FAQ says covers unlimited users, inventory, manufacturing, purchasing, traceability, warehouse management, the shop floor app, integrations, implementation, an implementation manager and a customer success manager, with no per-user charge. The Core plan from $299/month and the separately priced add-ons ($199, $249 and $149 a month) that the page listed until at least 23 September 2026 are no longer on it; the FAQ tells existing Standard, Professional, Professional Plus and Core customers that Katana will contact them about changes to their plan. Our hands-on test on 24 October 2026 still reached a Core checkout at $299 a month from inside a Free account, so whether new accounts can still buy Core in the app is not confirmed.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 24 October 2026 on the Free plan: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We imported two made-up products, exported them, updated one through the export file and opened the Core checkout without entering a card.
findings: Sign-up needed no card, call or integration; the onboarding took about ten steps and the phone number was optional. The account started on the Free plan at 0 of 30 items, with unlimited SKUs to try for 15 days.

We imported two products through the manual Products template, with EUR as base currency; the counter moved to 2 of 30 items. That template has no columns for a custom code, a date, tags, quantity, product state or attachments.

Settings > Data import > Products > Download current data returned an XLSX that we uploaded again with one changed note. Katana updated the existing products by their Katana ID: both IDs stayed the same and only that note changed.

Choosing Core at $299 a month came with three add-ons already ticked ($199, $199 and $149), which added $547 for $846 in fixed monthly costs shown as due today; usage was estimated separately and the route showed only dollars. We stopped at the card form.

Our three support questions in the in-app chat were answered within seconds by 'Katana • AI Agent': client data can be exported (attachments were not specifically confirmed), data is kept for up to six months after an account ends, and aggregated, anonymized data is used for research and improvement. We saw no human reply in that session.
Inviting a colleague at our own plus address left the invitation pending; all visibility and workflow permissions were switched on by default, admin rights were not.
not_tested: Cancelling (the account stays on the Free plan)
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
